transcript: Most people don't know it, but the more you stay home, the less you want to leave. And the more you stay, the heavier everything feels. You think you're resting, but you're actually draining the life out of yourself. Zen teaches that life is like water. When water flows, it stays pure. When it stops, it rots. You aren't recharging in that room. You are becoming a stagnant pond. In Zen, the self is not a noun. It is a verb. You are not a thing that exists. You are an act that happens. When you stop acting, the self doesn't rest. It stagnates. You feel heavy because you are carrying the weight of a life you aren't living. Remember this. The bird doesn't find its wings by sitting in the nest, dreaming of the sky. It finds them in the fall. If you wait until you feel ready to go outside, you will wait until your spirit becomes a statue. Look at the world through comfort, and every task seems like a mountain. Look at the world through Zen, and the mountain is just a path. Don't seek rest, seek flow, because a body in motion is a soul that is awake. If you've been feeling stuck like this, I wrote something for you. It's called The Way Back to Stillness. It's not just a book. It's a guide to clear your mind, reconnect with yourself, and finally feel at peace again. If you're ready to feel like yourself again, check the link on my profile.
